summary: Screw-pile front light of the Brewerton Channel range in the Patapsco River, lit 1868; demolished in 1924; its foundation light removed in 2015.

light.history: two lights from 1 November 1868; upper light discontinued 1 May 1879; fixed white changed to automatic flashing April 1915

structures.foundation: iron screw piles in six feet of water
structures.status: wooden tower demolished 1924; the screw-pile foundation carried an automatic light until it was removed in 2015

staffing.note: archive roster 1868 to 1915; head keeper William Raabe of Leading Point became keeper of both lights 16 April 1915

visit.note: The 1924 structure is gone; the 2015 solar-panel light is in the river (Chesapeake Chapter)

corrections.proposed: wooden tower demolished 1924; screw-pile foundation remained and carried an automatic light until 2015
corrections.why: The Chesapeake Chapter says the lighthouse was demolished in 1924 and the light on the old foundation was removed in 2015. The archive gives 1924 as discontinued and disposition as replaced with a steel pole. The record's 'standing' tower is not supported.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Congress appropriated the money in 1866 and construction ran through 1867 (Chesapeake Chapter; LighthouseFriends quoting the Board); both lights were first exhibited on 1 November 1868. The record's 1868 is correct. The earlier years in the record's conflict note are the appropriation and the start of construction.

The archive gives 1924 as discontinued and records a steel-pole replacement. The Chesapeake Chapter says the wooden lighthouse was demolished in 1924 and an automatic light was then placed on the screw-pile foundation, which carried that light until 2015. The record's 2015 date therefore refers to the foundation light, not the 1868 tower.

The Chesapeake Chapter says the judge ordered the landowner to receive $3,500 in damages (1890) and that Congress appropriated $4,500 in 1891 ($3,500 for the owner, $1,000 for the attorneys). LighthouseFriends gives $3,500 as the jury of condemnation's award for the easement between the two lights, paid to the owner in 1891. The story states both accounts and does not pick one.

The 1896 Board report entry (scan p. 351, labelled 1896 in the corpus) gives no date for the cutting; the Chesapeake Chapter and LighthouseFriends list it under 1897. The story says the Board's 1896 report records it and gives the 1897 dating of the two secondary sources.

The archive records a steel-pole replacement in 1924; the Chesapeake Chapter and LighthouseFriends say the superstructure was demolished and an automatic light installed on the screw-pile foundation. The story gives both accounts.

notes_for_editor: Place matched by name to the USLHS record Hawkins Point (Brewerton Channel) about 1 km from the station record's position (the tool first listed Leading Point and Hawkins Point as candidates; the Brewerton Channel name settles it). Roster: 17 lines from the archive, matching the record's count; all read from the archive place page. OCR tables: the Light-House Board 1891 entry is printed under item 476 (Leading Point) but describes the strip across Hawkins Point; the scan page is 446 and the printed page was not read. The 1891 and 1896 quotes are copied from OCR and checked by the checker. The Washington Herald and Atlanta Georgian pages are OCR text read through the newspaper tool; the Atlanta subhead is quoted as printed and not interpreted (it may count stevedores as a subset of the dead). The toll the Herald gave (fifty lives) is not checked against any other paper's total. Name variant: LighthouseFriends prints the 1889 landowner as Thomas O. Ghappell (a transcription error for Chappell); the Chesapeake Chapter has Thomas C. Chappell, and the 1890 judge's order names Chappell. The record's 'first_lit 1964' has no source in these pages and is not used. The record's 'tower standing' and the OSM note that the structure 'maps today' conflict with the 1924 demolition; OSM is probably showing the foundation. The Alum Chine damage to the light is cited to the Chesapeake Chapter, not to a newspaper. The Dawson Chemical plant that burned at Hawkins Point three miles from the blast (Atlanta Georgian) is not a lighthouse event and is not used. The Mrs. John Peterson entry and Hellen Isabella Waterworth are archive entries with no second source. No photos are proposed. Added for this check: LighthouseFriends files the July 1891 clearing under 1892 and the tree-cutting under 1897; the corpus labels the volumes 1891 (scan p. 446) and 1896 (scan p. 351), and the 1891 text reads 'In July, 1891', which the story quotes as the report's own date. The July 1888 storm month is not in any Board report the corpus holds (lhb has no hit), so the story gives the year as LighthouseFriends and the Chesapeake Chapter date it. The Georgian's 'Thirty Stevedores Killed' is quoted as printed; its text places the dead among the stevedores employed by the Joseph A. Foard Company, and the story does not read the subhead as a rival total. The Chesapeake Chapter calls the Alum Chine a freighter; the Herald and the Georgian call it a British steamer, and the story uses 'British steamer' with both newspapers cited.
